target.title: chore: sync canonical autoreview skill
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's bundled autoreview skill had drifted behind the canonical `openclaw/agent-skills` copy. It lacked custom Codex model defaults, fast-mode selection, newer reviewer engines, and later compatibility/isolation hardening.

## Why This Change Was Made

Synchronize `.agents/skills/autoreview` from the canonical shared skill, including `AUTOREVIEW_CODEX_MODEL`, `AUTOREVIEW_CODEX_SPEED`, repeatable Codex config overrides, deterministic tests, and preserved legacy Cursor aliases. The two source trees now match exactly.

## User Impact

Maintainers can set a private `AUTOREVIEW_CODEX_MODEL` value and `AUTOREVIEW_CODEX_SPEED=fast` in shell/launcher environment, or use an untracked repository-local environment loader such as `.envrc`. Autoreview does not create or own a defaults file.

Codex accepts the custom model name. Fast mode is requested as its `priority` service tier and only applies when that model's catalog metadata advertises support.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted change; no transcript attached.
- Canonical and bundled source trees compared identical, excluding generated Python bytecode.
- Skill manifest validation and skill-creator validation passed.
- Built-in autoreview self-tests passed.
- `python3 .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview_test.py` (16 tests).
- Hardening suite (14 tests).
- `cursor-agent` engine and binary compatibility aliases dry-run verified.
- Full branch autoreview with `gpt-5.5` fast mode: clean, confidence 0.82.
- Fresh `~/Projects/codex` pull at `be33f80bc65159c094ecd06bf155afa3061ce23d`; verified `codex-rs/protocol/src/config_types.rs:475`, `codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs:3558`, and `codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs:900`.
